scope: Local physical hand card launch continuity in the actual WPF table
changes: Visible local hand slots expose a presentation-only hand anchor; the battle layer matches only committed public card IDs from the local owner.
The layer caches last arranged visible hand geometry because state observers can remove a container before its public cue reaches the UI.
Each accepted flight copies only its rectangle into the existing transient TimedCue, without retaining a private card/control or changing command state.
The outgoing local face begins at the selected/lifted hand slot with full opacity and size, then follows the existing curved flight to its public landing.
Sorting the remaining hand does not move an accepted flight's source. Hidden/offscreen/unmatched/foreign cards retain the portrait fallback.
Motion off, collection reset, hand root replacement and unload clear the cached geometry; reload does not animate historical cues.
Native recording reuses the existing GIF timing writer with a centisecond parameter; the existing preview keeps its 80 ms timing.
A guarded focus prerequisite diagnostic was added after an existing native Cancel Enter check failed once; its assertions and input behavior were preserved.

baseline.issue: Accepted native Slash began as a small face at the portrait, instead of continuing from the selected hand slot.

filters: declaration and general library views protect private faces

nativeAssertions: Selection commits no command and starts no public flight.
Confirmation commits exactly once and removes the physical card from the visible hand.
The first artwork rectangle exactly matches the previously selected hand face and is fully opaque.
Sorting preserves the launch rectangle when a new frame is rendered.
Flight lands at the real bound public row face.
Rendering/sorting preserve all player-safe snapshots and accepted command count.
Saving/loading clears transient hand-flight state and its timer.
boundaryCoverage: Foreign owner cannot use a local hand slot even with a matching ID.
An unmatched public ID falls back to its actor portrait.
Offscreen/hidden hand cards fall back to the actor portrait.
Reset and motion toggles do not reuse removed cached cards.
Unload detaches observation, stops the timer and clears positions; load ignores historical cues.

motionRecording.note: Injected frame-clock WPF rendering recordings; not physical foreground acceptance or screen FPS.

routineFirst.failure: hand responses select exact cards and confirm through shared controls: native loaded cancel focus prerequisites failed.

focusStandaloneRetry.behavior: Exact loaded Cancel Enter path selected the native decline alternative once and preserved the selected Dodge payment boundary.

wpfRoutineRetry.source: All 37 Wpf filters imported from tools/VerificationScopes.psd1; same WPF routine order. Core was already passed and was not repeated.

validation.focusInvestigation: The initial focus prerequisite failure did not recur in standalone or same-scope WPF retry. Its cause is not established; this is not claimed as a product focus fix.

observedFollowUps: The public settled face is still visible while its outgoing flight is elsewhere; make the flight-to-static handoff show one card per play.
The captured bottom-right portrait attack trail also calls for broader playback/audio control-panel protection.
limitations: The new origin applies to matching visible local physical cards. A virtual/unmatched/offscreen card keeps the existing portrait source.
The response recording uses a fixed four-player rules fixture with placeholder portraits; the Slash recording uses the normal eight-player WPF table.
Code and rendered controls were checked; sustained human foreground play, multi-DPI and audio acceptance remain open.
Unrelated dirty work, Core rules, replay/content versions and command commit/recovery were preserved in this batch.

cleanup.reason: Earlier exact-path cleanup was blocked by policy. Compatible outputs were reused; no deletion retry is permitted. Exact retained paths remain queued.
